Database-backed health endpoint (Spring Boot Actuator)
recipes.snippet:
Spring Boot 3.4 and newer including 4.x with spring-boot-starter-actuator. The built-in /actuator/health already does what OPS-002 asks: with a DataSource it includes the `db` indicator (it must obtain a connection), the overall status DOWN maps to HTTP 503 and UP to 200 by default, and with show-details=never the body is only {"status":"UP"} or {"status":"DOWN"} (Boot 4 adds a harmless "groups":["liveness","readiness"] list; no components, versions or driver names). Do not set any `management.endpoint.health.status.http-mapping.*` property: defining one switches off the default DOWN -> 503 mapping. Without a database, add your own HealthIndicator for the critical dependency (a failing one makes the whole endpoint DOWN -> 503). Spring Security's default Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store covers "never cached"; without Spring Security add the header in a filter.
### file: src/main/resources/application.properties
# only health is exposed over HTTP, and the /actuator discovery page (it lists links) is off (SEC-035)
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoints.web.discovery.enabled=false
# no component tree, no details: nothing about the database engine or versions leaks (OPS-002)
management.endpoint.health.show-details=never
management.endpoint.health.show-components=never
# fail fast when the database is down: Hikari's connection-timeout is in ms (minimum 250), default 30000
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=2000
### file: src/main/java/com/example/web/SecurityConfig.java (only if you restrict other routes; the headers recipe uses permitAll)
.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
    .requestMatchers("/actuator/health").permitAll() // monitors call it without a session
    .anyRequest().authenticated())
### file: curl-checks.sh
# up:   curl -i http://localhost:8080/actuator/health   -> 200 {"status":"UP"}
# down: stop the database, repeat                        -> 503 {"status":"DOWN"} within about 2 seconds
